forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: Peak daily transits during Jun 10-22 reached approximately 35 vessels (June 21) but collapsed to approximately 12 by June 22 after Iran's military declared the strait closed on June 20 (Iran's foreign ministry issued a contradictory statement; CENTCOM disputed the closure claim). IMF PortWatch data through June 14 showed 0% of pre-war volume; even at the June 19 high of approximately 20 tankers, the 7-day moving average remained well below 15/day. The 50/day threshold is structurally blocked by: (a) Iran's contested re-closure June 20; (b) active mines requiring 40-50 more days for clearance; (c) P&I insurers still applying war-risk surcharges. p adjusted to 0.10 (rounded from 0.07 to avoid false precision). Judge flag: human should verify PortWatch 7-day AIS aggregate for June 15-22.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: No second or third reading has occurred as of June 23. However, the political calculus has shifted: Netanyahu's coalition at approximately 60 seats per polling aggregates; Haredi parties (Shas, UTJ) actively pushing for a September election date while Netanyahu prefers October. All major parties are aligned on dissolution itself; the date dispute is a secondary intra-coalition negotiation, not a blocking veto. A Times of Israel report from mid-June described Netanyahu as potentially pushing final readings 'within days.' Three weeks remain to the July 15 horizon. Probability nudged from 0.45 to 0.55. Judge flag: if no vote by June 30, review downward.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: Weekly cadence: last_reasoned_at updated to 2026-06-23 to document that the Monday cadence rule was applied consciously — no intra-week p-move permitted. Background for Sunday June 29 audit: polling shows coalition at ~50 seats vs opposition ~60; dissolution bill advancing (106-0 first reading June 2). DA argued for OBE retirement; Judge rejected on procedural grounds — forced retirement on a Monday violates cadence rule. Full Sunday audit required June 29.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran conclude a written final agreement (or explicitly extend the MOU framework beyond 60 days) before EOD 2026-08-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: The June 17 MOU opens a 60-day window (expires approximately August 16-17) for a final deal. The Switzerland round June 21-22 established four working groups and a roadmap. However, Iran and US have conflicting claims on IAEA access, Hormuz reopening pace, and sanction termination sequencing. Historical precedent (JCPOA took 20+ months) weighs against completion inside 60 days. Vance's 'good foundation' characterization is positive but not binding. New forecast seeded at p=0.30.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if TIER1 reports a signed, publicly announced comprehensive final agreement between US and Iran OR a formal joint statement by both parties explicitly extending the MOU framework for further negotiations beyond August 17, before EOD 2026-08-17.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera/NBC) OR joint statement by US State Dept and Iran MFA.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Working group progress reports without a signed instrument = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; unilateral claims of agreement without the other party's confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will at least two of the four US-Iran working groups (Sanctions, Nuclear, Reconstruction, Monitoring) convene a first formal session before EOD 2026-07-07?

However, Iran's FM spokesman Baghaei disputed Vance's characterization of IAEA commitments on June 22, introducing material uncertainty about the Nuclear Affairs working group timeline. Trump threats introduced additional procedural uncertainty. Judge flag: if IAEA inspectors do not arrive within the week following June 22, probability should be reviewed downward before July 7. forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if TIER1 reports that at least two of the four named working groups have each held at least one formal session with named participants, before EOD 2026-07-07.
